questions.text: Which symbol denote derived attributes in ER Model?
questions.solution:
In ER notation a derived attribute (computed from others, like age from date of birth) is drawn as a dashed ellipse. Multivalued attributes use a double ellipse, and key attributes are underlined.

Answer: Dashed ellipse

questions.text:
[latex]\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|} \hline \textbf{Employee} & \textbf{Department} & \textbf{OT allowance} \\ \hline \text{RAMA} & \text{Mechanical} & \text{5000} \\\hline \text{GOPI} & \text{Electrical} & \text{2000} \\\hline \text{SINDHU} & \text{Computer} & \text{4000} \\\hline \text{MAHESH} & \text{Civil} & \text{1500} \\\hline \end{array}[/latex]
What is the output of the following SQL query?
 select count(*) from 
    ((select Employee, Department from Overtime_allowance) 
    natural join 
    (select Department, OT_allowance from Overtime_allowance) 
    as T);
questions.solution:
The two subqueries are joined on their common column, Department. Each department appears once, so each (Employee, Department) row matches exactly one (Department, OT_allowance) row: 4 rows.

Answer: 4

questions.text: Which of the following concurrency control protocol ensures both conflict and free from deadlock? ,
questions.solution:
Timestamp ordering decides conflicts by timestamps (older first), so schedules are conflict serializable. Transactions never wait for locks (they are aborted and restarted instead), so there is no deadlock. Basic 2PL guarantees serializability but can deadlock.

Answer: Time stamp ordering
